incident.title: Checkout requests failing with HTTP 500
symptoms: Checkout error rate above 20% since about 10:05 UTC

tasks.goal: Pull checkout-svc error logs and metrics (HTTP 500 rate, latency, saturation, top exception types and stack traces) for the incident window. Identify the exact onset time of the error spike around 10:05 UTC and any failing downstream calls.

List deploys, config changes, feature-flag flips and infra changes to checkout-svc and its direct dependencies (especially payment-related services) between 09:45 and 10:30 UTC. Flag any change that lands just before the 10:05 onset.

Map the upstream and downstream dependencies of checkout-svc, such as payment gateway, inventory, DB and cache. Find past incidents with similar checkout HTTP 500 or payment page error patterns, and note their root causes.

Synthesize findings from logs/metrics, change history, and the dependency graph and past incidents. Produce ranked competing root-cause hypotheses for the checkout-svc HTTP 500 spike starting around 10:05 UTC. For each hypothesis, give supporting and contradicting evidence, confidence, and the next verification step.

Establish exact onset ordering. Pull checkout-svc error_rate_pct and node_cpu_pct at 1-minute resolution, plus request rate if available. Confirm that errors stay at the ~0.4% baseline until after the 10:02 v2.3.1 deploy. Check whether CPU rises only after the error spike or was already elevated before 10:02.

Test h3. Pull pricing-db error and latency metrics, ERROR/WARN logs, and any deploy, config, schema or migration changes. Determine whether pricing-db began returning null, missing or errored discount or price records around 10:00-10:05, independent of the checkout-svc deploy.

Revise the hypotheses with the new findings. The Critic said: h1 is well supported. A checkout-svc v2.3.1 'Discount engine refactor' deploy at 10:02 is followed by an NPE in v2.3.1 PriceCalculator.applyDiscount at 10:04:51 and by 500s on POST /checkout. Error rate went from 0.4% at 10:00 to 23.5% at 10:06, and a past incident followed the same pattern. h4 (search-svc TTL) has no dependency path and fails to explain an NPE in discount code, so it can stay low. Three things are weaker than the ranking implies.

1. **Onset timing.** The error-rate metric has only two samples, 10:00 and 10:06. An onset before 10:02 cannot be excluded, and that would break the deploy causality. The CPU reading is also a single sample at 10:06, so h2's 'CPU is a side effect' claim is assumed, not shown. A 1-minute series would settle both questions.

2. **The pricing-db alternative (h3) was never tested.** An NPE in applyDiscount is exactly what you would see if pricing-db started returning null or missing discount rows. The deploy and the data change could also interact: v2.3.1 dereferencing a field that was always occasionally null. pricing-db logs, metrics and schema or migration changes were never queried. Absence of pricing-db references in checkout logs is weak evidence, because an NPE on a null row would not name the DB. Rollback is still a reasonable mitigation either way. However, if pricing-db data changed, rollback alone may not restore the baseline, or a later re-release would fail again.

3. **Smaller evidence gaps.** These are lower priority and unlikely to change the ranking unless the first two checks surprise:
- log:inc01:0005 is missing.
- dependency:inc01:0003 is missing.
- Three ERROR lines against a 23.5% error rate.

facts.statement: checkout-svc deployed v2.3.1 ("Discount engine refactor") at 2026-11-10T10:02:00Z.
The first ERROR log in the window is a NullPointerException in PriceCalculator.applyDiscount (v2.3.1) at 2026-11-10T10:04:51Z.
The first logged POST /checkout 500 caused by NullPointerException in PriceCalculator.applyDiscount is at 2026-11-10T10:05:07Z, and another identical 500 is logged at 2026-11-10T10:07:02Z.
checkout-svc error_rate_pct was 0.4 at 2026-11-10T10:00:00Z and 23.5 at 2026-11-10T10:06:00Z.
checkout-svc node_cpu_pct was 94.0 at 2026-11-10T10:06:00Z.
checkout-svc's downstream dependencies in the service graph are payments-svc and pricing-db.

The returned ERROR logs for checkout-svc in the window contain only NullPointerException failures in PriceCalculator.applyDiscount; none of the returned error lines reference payments-svc or pricing-db.

assumptions.statement: The error-rate onset is between 10:00 and 10:06 UTC, and the first NPE log at 10:04:51 is consistent with the ~10:05 onset in the report.
assumptions.basis: Metric samples are sparse (10:00 and 10:06 only), so the exact onset minute cannot be read from metrics alone.
assumptions.how_to_verify: Pull error_rate_pct at 1-minute resolution for 10:00-10:10 and compare with the first NPE timestamp.

assumptions.statement: The v2.3.1 deploy at 10:02 is the trigger for the NPE spike.
assumptions.basis: Temporal ordering (deploy 10:02, first NPE 10:04:51, error-rate jump by 10:06) and the NPE message naming v2.3.1 code. This is correlation plus a plausible code path, not a confirmed cause.
assumptions.how_to_verify: Diff v2.3.1 against the prior version for applyDiscount null handling; check whether reverting to the prior version clears the NPE; check for a null input (e.g., a discount or price record) that v2.3.1 newly dereferences.

assumptions.statement: The CPU spike (94%) is a side effect of errors or retries, not a cause of the 500s.
assumptions.basis: Single CPU sample at 10:06 with no baseline or saturation trend returned.
assumptions.how_to_verify: Pull node_cpu_pct and request-rate metrics for 09:45-10:30 and check whether CPU rises after the deploy or after the error spike.

assumptions.statement: The downstream services payments-svc and pricing-db are not implicated.
assumptions.basis: No error logs from checkout-svc referencing them were returned. Their own logs and metrics were not queried, so this is an absence of evidence.
assumptions.how_to_verify: Query logs and error metrics for payments-svc and pricing-db over 09:45-10:30 and check for timeouts or 5xx responses.

assumptions.statement: Latency and saturation metrics beyond CPU, and stack traces, are not available in this data.
assumptions.basis: The unfiltered metrics call returned only error_rate_pct and node_cpu_pct. Log payloads contain messages only, with no stack traces.
assumptions.how_to_verify: Query p50/p99 latency, memory, and thread or connection pool metrics by name, and fetch full log entries (or traces) for the NPE events.

assumptions.statement: The log stream may be incomplete. Evidence IDs jump from log:inc01:0004 to 0006, and the WARN query returned no rows.
assumptions.basis: The ERROR query returned three entries with omitted=0, which leaves a missing ID (0005) unexplained. The WARN query returned an empty evidence list with no error status.
assumptions.how_to_verify: Re-run the ERROR query for the same window and check whether an entry with ID 0005 appears; confirm the logging pipeline has no drops for checkout-svc.

assumptions.statement: Error logs in this window only show NPEs; other 500 causes may exist without logged errors.
assumptions.basis: Only three ERROR entries were returned and all are the same NPE. The 23.5% error rate suggests more failing requests than the logs show.
assumptions.how_to_verify: Compare request-level 500 counts with the logged error count, and check access logs or traces for 500 responses without a matching ERROR line.

hypotheses.summary: The checkout-svc v2.3.1 'Discount engine refactor' deploy at 10:02 UTC introduced a null-handling defect in PriceCalculator.applyDiscount. The NPE makes POST /checkout return 500. This includes the interaction case the Critic raised: v2.3.1 may now dereference a discount or price field from pricing-db that was always occasionally null. In that case the code change is still the trigger. Support: the deploy precedes the first NPE (10:04:51) and the first logged 500 (10:05:07). The NPE is in v2.3.1 code. A past incident matches this pattern (a discount null bug after a release, fixed by rollback). Gaps remain. The c1.1 re-query again returned only the 10:00 (0.4%) and 10:06 (23.5%) samples, so an onset between 10:00 and 10:02 is still not excluded. The earliest error evidence is the 10:04:51 NPE, which is after the deploy. There are also only three ERROR lines against a 23.5% error rate. Next step: get 1-minute error_rate_pct for 09:45-10:10 and diff applyDiscount null handling between v2.3.1 and the prior version. Then roll back and confirm the error rate returns to the ~0.4% baseline.

Node CPU saturation, possibly from a noisy-neighbour batch job like the past incident, causes checkout requests to fail. CPU was 94% at 10:06, when errors were high. c1.1 confirmed that this is the only CPU sample, so there is no evidence on whether CPU rose before or after 10:02. Against this: every logged error is an application NPE, not a timeout or resource error, and the past noisy-neighbour incident caused latency, not 500s. Next step: pull 1-minute node_cpu_pct and request rate for 09:45-10:30, and check co-located workload scheduling.

pricing-db, a direct checkout dependency, started returning null or missing discount or price records (for example after a data change or a schema migration done outside the deploy tool). applyDiscount then dereferences the null and throws an NPE. If this is the cause, a rollback alone may not restore baseline. c1.2 queried pricing-db, and every result came back empty: metrics, logs at all levels, and scoped deploys. Empty is not the same as healthy, because missing ingestion looks identical. Migrations made outside the deploy pipeline would not appear either. So h3 is neither confirmed nor refuted. Weighing against it: the NPE names v2.3.1 code, and a checkout-svc code change sits right before the first error. Next step: check pricing-db migration and DDL audit history, confirm pricing-db logs and metrics are being ingested, and inspect the discount rows involved in the failing requests.

The search-svc cache.ttl_seconds change from 300 to 60 at 09:58 UTC raised load on a shared component and indirectly broke checkout. This is unlikely. search-svc has no edge to checkout-svc or pricing-db in the returned graph, and the errors are discount-code NPEs, not cache or load failures. The missing dependency:inc01:0003 edge leaves a small chance of an unseen path.

h1 is well supported. A checkout-svc v2.3.1 'Discount engine refactor' deploy at 10:02 is followed by an NPE in v2.3.1 PriceCalculator.applyDiscount at 10:04:51 and by 500s on POST /checkout. Error rate went from 0.4% at 10:00 to 23.5% at 10:06, and a past incident followed the same pattern. h4 (search-svc TTL) has no dependency path and fails to explain an NPE in discount code, so it can stay low. Three things are weaker than the ranking implies.

1. **Onset timing.** The error-rate metric has only two samples, 10:00 and 10:06. An onset before 10:02 cannot be excluded, and that would break the deploy causality. The CPU reading is also a single sample at 10:06, so h2's 'CPU is a side effect' claim is assumed, not shown. A 1-minute series would settle both questions.

2. **The pricing-db alternative (h3) was never tested.** An NPE in applyDiscount is exactly what you would see if pricing-db started returning null or missing discount rows. The deploy and the data change could also interact: v2.3.1 dereferencing a field that was always occasionally null. pricing-db logs, metrics and schema or migration changes were never queried. Absence of pricing-db references in checkout logs is weak evidence, because an NPE on a null row would not name the DB. Rollback is still a reasonable mitigation either way. However, if pricing-db data changed, rollback alone may not restore the baseline, or a later re-release would fail again.

3. **Smaller evidence gaps.** These are lower priority and unlikely to change the ranking unless the first two checks surprise:
- log:inc01:0005 is missing.
- dependency:inc01:0003 is missing.
- Three ERROR lines against a 23.5% error rate.

follow_ups.goal: Establish exact onset ordering. Pull checkout-svc error_rate_pct and node_cpu_pct at 1-minute resolution, plus request rate if available. Confirm that errors stay at the ~0.4% baseline until after the 10:02 v2.3.1 deploy. Check whether CPU rises only after the error spike or was already elevated before 10:02.

Test h3. Pull pricing-db error and latency metrics, ERROR/WARN logs, and any deploy, config, schema or migration changes. Determine whether pricing-db began returning null, missing or errored discount or price records around 10:00-10:05, independent of the checkout-svc deploy.

critic_reviews.critique:
h1 holds up and should stay on top. Five points support this.

1. **Timing and code path.** The v2.3.1 'Discount engine refactor' deploy at 10:02 comes before every piece of error evidence. Three ERROR lines from the full-window query are all the same NPE in PriceCalculator.applyDiscount, they name v2.3.1 code, and the earliest is at 10:04:51. Nothing was logged at ERROR before 10:02. The code path matches the deploy's stated scope.
2. **Precedent.** The match with past:inc01:0002 (discount null bug after a release, fixed by rollback) is strong.
3. **Onset between 10:00 and 10:02.** This gap is real. But c1.1 already re-queried and got the same sparse samples, so another metrics pull will most likely fail the same way. It would spend most of the remaining 8 tool calls for little value. Even if an onset at 10:01 were somehow shown, an NPE in v2.3.1-only code could not come from the prior version. The ordering argument therefore rests on the code path, not just on the metric samples.
4. **The missing log:inc01:0005.** By sequence it falls between 10:05:07 and 10:07:02. That is after the deploy, so it cannot move the onset. The 3-lines-versus-23.5% mismatch looks like sampled or deduplicated logging, not evidence of a second failure mode.
5. **Competing hypotheses.**
   - **h2 (CPU).** Correctly ranked low. The errors are application NPEs, not timeouts, and the noisy-neighbour precedent produced latency, not 500s.
   - **h4 (search-svc).** Correctly ranked low. It has no graph path and its failure signature does not match.
   - **h3 (pricing-db).** This is the only competitor that matters. It is mostly absorbed into h1 as the interaction case: the code change is still the trigger even if the null data is old. pricing-db returned empty results everywhere, and that cannot be resolved with the tools available, since the deploy tool does not see DDL audit or migrations.

The practical consequence of h3 is already captured in the remediation plan. Roll back, then confirm the error rate returns to about 0.4%. If it does not, pricing-db data becomes the lead. That rollback is itself the decisive test, and it is cheaper and more conclusive than any query left in the budget.

One remaining recommendation is to keep confidence near 0.75 rather than raise it. The onset gap and pricing-db's empty telemetry are not closed, and the rollback outcome should be reported as confirmation. No further investigation is likely to change the ranking.

ranked_hypotheses.summary: The checkout-svc v2.3.1 'Discount engine refactor' deploy at 10:02 UTC introduced a null-handling defect in PriceCalculator.applyDiscount. The NPE makes POST /checkout return 500. This includes the interaction case the Critic raised: v2.3.1 may now dereference a discount or price field from pricing-db that was always occasionally null. In that case the code change is still the trigger. Support: the deploy precedes the first NPE (10:04:51) and the first logged 500 (10:05:07). The NPE is in v2.3.1 code. A past incident matches this pattern (a discount null bug after a release, fixed by rollback). Gaps remain. The c1.1 re-query again returned only the 10:00 (0.4%) and 10:06 (23.5%) samples, so an onset between 10:00 and 10:02 is still not excluded. The earliest error evidence is the 10:04:51 NPE, which is after the deploy. There are also only three ERROR lines against a 23.5% error rate. Next step: get 1-minute error_rate_pct for 09:45-10:10 and diff applyDiscount null handling between v2.3.1 and the prior version. Then roll back and confirm the error rate returns to the ~0.4% baseline.

pricing-db, a direct checkout dependency, started returning null or missing discount or price records (for example after a data change or a schema migration done outside the deploy tool). applyDiscount then dereferences the null and throws an NPE. If this is the cause, a rollback alone may not restore baseline. c1.2 queried pricing-db, and every result came back empty: metrics, logs at all levels, and scoped deploys. Empty is not the same as healthy, because missing ingestion looks identical. Migrations made outside the deploy pipeline would not appear either. So h3 is neither confirmed nor refuted. Weighing against it: the NPE names v2.3.1 code, and a checkout-svc code change sits right before the first error. Next step: check pricing-db migration and DDL audit history, confirm pricing-db logs and metrics are being ingested, and inspect the discount rows involved in the failing requests.

Node CPU saturation, possibly from a noisy-neighbour batch job like the past incident, causes checkout requests to fail. CPU was 94% at 10:06, when errors were high. c1.1 confirmed that this is the only CPU sample, so there is no evidence on whether CPU rose before or after 10:02. Against this: every logged error is an application NPE, not a timeout or resource error, and the past noisy-neighbour incident caused latency, not 500s. Next step: pull 1-minute node_cpu_pct and request rate for 09:45-10:30, and check co-located workload scheduling.

The search-svc cache.ttl_seconds change from 300 to 60 at 09:58 UTC raised load on a shared component and indirectly broke checkout. This is unlikely. search-svc has no edge to checkout-svc or pricing-db in the returned graph, and the errors are discount-code NPEs, not cache or load failures. The missing dependency:inc01:0003 edge leaves a small chance of an unseen path.
